page: Microsoft Azure E32-16ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained vCPU profile. Powered by the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, this instance operates at a maximum clock frequency of 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 16 vCPUs across 8 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory footprint stands at 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a dense ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Local temporary storage is provided via an integrated 1888 GB NVMe SSD. No dedicated graphics processing units are present on this virtual instance.

Benchmark data highlights exceptionally strong single-core CPU execution. Tests including stress-ng single-core, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all registered within the top tier of evaluated systems. Geekbench single-core scores reached 2441.0, and text processing operations reached 3149.0, both placing in the top ten percent. Multi-core performance scales predictably to the 16 vCPU limit, posting average tier results across stress-ng multi-core (28086.9) and Geekbench multi-core (13544.0). PassMark memory testing achieved a strong tier score of 2834.9, supported by an uncached read memory bandwidth of 51.55 GB/s and write bandwidth of 34.27 GB/s.

In runtime and application-level workloads, the instance demonstrates balanced throughput. Redis SET benchmarks yielded 27.21 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measured 26.29 GB/s. For CPU-based language model inference, execution remains competitive on compact parameter architectures, reaching 387.72 tokens per second for text generation on a 135M model. However, performance degrades substantially when testing larger models, showing 5.48 tokens per second on 70B prompt processing without hardware acceleration.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, the constrained core count lowers per-core software licensing costs while retaining the memory capacity and fast local NVMe storage of a larger 32-vCPU chassis. This makes the E32-16ads_v7 optimal for memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caches, data analytics pipelines, and ETL processing workloads that require high RAM capacity per thread without paying for unneeded CPU licenses.
description: Microsoft Azure E32-16ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs on 8 AMD EPYC 9V45 physical cores operating up to 4.5 GHz. Designed on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding an expansive 16.0 GB of memory per vCPU. The instance includes a bundled 1888 GB NVMe SSD for fast local scratch space, though it lacks discrete GPU acceleration. Benchmark measurements show top-tier single-threaded CPU speed, reflected in Geekbench single-core results of 2441.0 and rapid text and compression throughput. Multi-core compute and memory bandwidth maintain steady mid-tier outputs, including 27.21 million Redis SET operations per second. By pairing a high-capacity memory footprint with a constrained CPU allocation, the E32-16ads_v7 provides strong resource density and qualitative licensing efficiency for large memory-bound databases, caching layers, and high-memory analytics workloads.
